solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In bitter enmity, stupidly staged grand war

indicators.note: done stupidly, the letters of the three words are thrown together in a senseless new order

parts.note: these three words supply the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly stages a great war out of bitter hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties openly hostile and ready to fight, as if their blades were already unsheathed.

clue.text: Scientific type collecting a second prize thus, is content, finally

parts.note: taken as written
a trophy is a prize awarded to a winner
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as copied exactly
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word content, its last letter only

parts.note: the word content, of which only the end letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A scientist pockets a runner-up award and declares themselves satisfied with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collecting' simply joins the definition to the long chain of pieces. 'Content' looks like an adjective meaning satisfied, but only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrophysicist is a scientist studying the physics of stars, planets and other bodies in space.

clue.text: Rebuilt citadel, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a building that is rebuilt is put together again, so the letters of the fortress word are reassembled

parts.note: the fortress word supplies the seven letters to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A fortress is reconstructed, described in a figurative way of putting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as the stock phrase meaning so to speak, but 'manner of speaking' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional or social variety of a language, literally a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Keep in Conservative with less sense who shouldn't be in party?

parts.note: to gate a pupil is to confine them to school grounds as a punishment
rasher means more rash, so showing less good sense

explanation.surface: A castle keep held by the Tories and someone foolish who has no business being at the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' suggests a castle tower, but 'keep in' is the verb gate, a British school punishment of being kept within bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatecrasher is an uninvited guest who forces their way into a social event.

clue.text: Unqualified driver not getting start in lucrative job

indicators.note: the driver word loses its opening letter, the start it does not get

parts.note: a learner driver has not yet passed the driving test

explanation.surface: A learner driver fails to get started on a well-paid job.
explanation.definitionFit: In British idiom a nice little earner is a profitable sideline or job that brings in money.

clue.text: Instant record of game's exciting

parts.note: snap is a simple card game, here with its possessive s
hot can mean thrilling or exciting, as in a hot property

explanation.surface: A quick account of a match that was thrilling to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a photograph taken quickly, capturing a single moment as a visual record.

clue.text: Doctor's trying, but oddly deficient

definitions.note: the definition is the verb doctor, falsify; the 's stands for is, joining it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the word is lacking its odd-numbered letters, so only the second, fourth and sixth remain

parts.note: the word trying, whose even letters survive once the odd ones go

explanation.surface: A doctor is making an effort but strangely falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig something, such as an election, is to falsify or tamper with it dishonestly.

clue.text: Calculate to satisfactorily finish exercise

definitions.meaning: first sense: to work a sum out
second sense: things ... when they end well
third sense: a session of physical training

explanation.surface: Plan your fitness routine so that it ends well.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of the same phrase are strung together; 'to' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers solving a problem and turning out well, and as one noun it is a gym session.

clue.text: Container of explosive ignited for spectacular revolution

definitions.meaning: the firework is a case packed with gunpowder that is set alight
it spins round on a pin, showering sparks: a revolution in the rotating sense, not a political uprising

explanation.surface: A bomb is set off to launch a dramatic political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests overthrowing a government; here it is simply spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: This spinning firework, named after the martyr's spiked wheel, rotates on a pin while burning brightly.

clue.text: One vehicle or another sent back in right direction

indicators.note: sending the cart back means its letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a second vehicle, a cart
to the right, i.e. TO with R for right

explanation.surface: One vehicle or another is returned and redirected the correct way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In right direction' is the phrase to R(ight).
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a heavy motor vehicle used for pulling farm machinery.

clue.text: This African country has aluminium where another has nickel, primarily

indicators.note: where marks the spot in the other country's name at which one element swaps for the other
the second has marks what the other country holds in that spot, the element now replaced
primarily says the swap happens at the very front of the name

parts.note: another African country, Nigeria

explanation.surface: A chemistry-flavoured comparison of two African nations by their metals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ni and Al are the chemical symbols for nickel and aluminium; swap the opening Ni of one neighbour's name for Al.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a large North African country on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Poet's work pronounced outstanding

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is heard spoken, sounding the same as another spelling

parts.note: a debt still outstanding is owed; the reversed run of the answer across these words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A poet's piece is declared to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise, but it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, typically addressed to a person or thing, so it is a poet's composition.

clue.text: Cotton cape Ethel chose, in need of alteration

indicators.note: a garment needing alteration must be remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the woman's name and the verb together supply ten letters to rework

explanation.surface: Ethel picked a cotton cape that needs taking in by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the map abbreviation for cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecloth is a loosely woven, light cotton fabric, originally used for wrapping cheese.

clue.text: Stake he secured in company plan that's put together to promote growth

definitions.text: that's put together to promote growth

indicators.note: the stake and he are held fast inside the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
a stake is a post driven into the ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stake is fixed in place as part of a company's scheme for expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests business expansion, which fits company and plan, but the growth is in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A compost heap is a pile of garden waste built up to rot down into fertiliser that helps plants grow.

clue.text: Contractor who's paid money to butcher

definitions.meaning: this one takes a contract on a person's life, not on building work
the job is killing, not cutting meat in a shop

explanation.surface: A tradesman hired and paid to do work for a meat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'contract' in underworld slang is an order to kill someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a professional killer hired by others to murder a target for payment.

clue.text: Regular traveller who reduces time, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first sense: someone travelling daily between home and work
second sense: one who commutes a prison sentence, reducing it

explanation.walkthrough: To commute a sentence is to replace it with a lighter one, so a prisoner serves less time.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily rail passenger and an official lightening a punishment share this agent noun from the verb meaning exchange.

clue.text: Person who provides topical information about ale

parts.note: porter is a dark brown beer brewed from roasted malt

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps people up to date on the subject of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and presents news on current events.

clue.text: Insulted Labour leader seen outside

indicators.note: the seen word goes outside, wrapping round the party's first letter

parts.note: something sighted has been seen

indicators.note: the leader of the word Labour is its opening letter

parts.note: the party name, whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: The Labour party chief was insulted by those looking on from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' suggests a politician, but it is just the first letter of Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slighted is to be snubbed or treated with disrespect, a close synonym of offended.

clue.text: The writer is succeeded by a friend in religious office

indicators.note: what comes after follows on, so the setter's phrase is put first and the friend after

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves: I am, shortened
taken as written
mate is a British word for a friend

explanation.surface: The setter is followed by a friend into a post in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the position or office of an imam, the leader of prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Turned heads, being sweet

indicators.note: turned here means each head is flipped round, so the pair is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: nob is slang for the head; two of them make heads

explanation.surface: People looked round because something was so charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned heads' reads as attracting attention; it is a slang word for head, doubled and reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small sweet or chocolate confection.

clue.text: Don't dilly-dally crossing line in city in UK

indicators.note: the hurry-up phrase crosses over the line, taking it inside

parts.note: the instruction be fast, i.e. hurry up

explanation.surface: Hurry through when crossing a line in a British city.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: White wine from area found in pubs and clubs

indicators.note: the area is found inside, sitting within the pubs and clubs

parts.note: bars are drinking places

explanation.surface: A white wine sourced from a district's drinking establishments.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the card abbreviation for clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux from the commune of that name in the Sauternes district.

clue.text: Unusually gifted person originally ordered into cavalry

indicators.note: the letters as originally ordered must be put in a different arrangement

parts.note: these two words supply exactly the eleven letters needed

explanation.surface: A remarkable individual was first commanded to join the mounted troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered into cavalry' reads as a military posting; the two words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant claims a supernatural gift of perceiving the future or things beyond normal senses.

clue.text: It's initially legislated at Westminster

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three following words

parts.note: the three words whose opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: Parliament in Westminster is where the thing is first passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute or rule passed by Parliament becomes the law of the land.

clue.text: Claret's possibly this shade of red

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word could be rearranged into another one

parts.note: the wine word with its possessive s gives seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wine might well be described by a particular red colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is also a name for a purplish red, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red colour with a slightly orange tinge.

clue.text: Conclusions reached in trial, so accept one's fate

indicators.note: the conclusions of the words are their final letters

explanation.surface: After the verdict at a court case, the defendant must accept what comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusions reached in trial' sounds like a jury verdict, but it means the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Your lot is your destiny or fortune in life, as in accepting one's lot.

clue.text: Part of cross-reference for ongoing loss of liquid assets

wordplay.note: a cross-reference directs the reader to look at a numbered leaf of the book, as in 'see p. 12'

explanation.surface: A bookkeeping footnote referring to a steady drain on cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid assets' means cash, but here the definition is a slow leak of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow escape of fluid through a porous material or small openings.

clue.text: Reform never restricting trade union with excellent financial backing

indicators.note: the rearranged word confines the union abbreviation within it
to reform is to reshape, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word never supplies the five letters to be reshaped
capital is an old-fashioned British word for excellent

explanation.surface: A political call for union reform paired with first-class funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new or risky businesses in exchange for a share of ownership.
